facts.fact: FaydaVerse's director says it provides identity verification to institutions, using one-time passwords, and has charged fees for it since August 2026.
The director says identity verification is available to government institutions, private companies and start-ups, and that banks are charged fees for it.

facts.fact: The FaydaVerse director says its work is governed by the Personal Data Protection Act and that one-time passwords are used for verification in accordance with it.
The FaydaVerse director says its work is governed by the Digital Identity Act.

ETH.note: Registration with witnesses for disabled people is enrolment inclusion, not accessible information or digital services.
Nothing on government payments to people.
Gives more than 52 million registered but no population or share, and the 40 per cent without proof of identity is a study figure, not enrolment.

Farmers' profiles work with the Agricultural Transformation Institute is not stated as a register keyed on the ID number.

facts.fact: The FaydaVerse director says more than 52 million citizens have registered for the national ID, which uses a 16-digit identification number, with 15,000 registration machines.
The FaydaVerse director says banks and other institutions verify customers' identities against the national ID, with fees charged since August 2026.
